citation: Al Tfaily F, Ghalmane Z, Brahmia MA, Hazimeh H, Jaber A, Zghal M. Graph-based federated learning approach for intrusion detection in IoT networks. Scientific Reports 15:41264, 2025. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-25175-1
url_read: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-25175-1 (read via web text extraction; cross-checked with PDF copy https://d-nb.info/1387602233/34)

A1.evidence: Results > Experimental setup: 'The dataset was partitioned across five simulated clients...'; no train/test split stated in Methods or Experimental setup.

A2.evidence: Temporal GAT analyzes 'timing patterns, traffic bursts, and connection sequences' (Methods); how graphs/windows are built from flows and how data are split is not stated.

A3.evidence: No scaling/encoding procedure stated in Methods (Client-side processing) or Experimental setup.

A4.evidence: Only relative statement: 'requires 25-30% fewer federation rounds'; no number of rounds or local epochs given (Experimental setup lists hidden dims, heads, dropout only).

A5.evidence: Experimental setup: 'Evaluation included centralized GAT, GraphSAGE, FedLSTM, a basic federated GNN, and a FedGATSage variant' — no statement on shared rounds/epochs.

A6.evidence: Table 1: 'Comparison of performance metrics across centralized and federated approaches for NF-ToN-IoT and CIC-ToN-IoT' — authors' own baselines; published numbers cited only in Discussion, not as baselines.

A7.evidence: 'Metrics included accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro F1 score'; 'FedGATSage achieved 78.58% balanced accuracy on the NF-ToN-IoT dataset'.

A8.evidence: Experimental setup: 'partitioned across five simulated clients with balanced attack distributions and network heterogeneity. Client sizes varied by up to 40% and class prevalence varied by 25%' — partition method not specified.

A9.evidence: No repeated runs, seeds, dispersion or statistical tests stated (Results, Experimental setup).

A10.evidence: NF-ToN-IoT and CIC-ToN-IoT evaluated separately; no cross-dataset evaluation.

A11.evidence: Code availability: 'Source code is available at: https://github.com/Fouad-AlTfaily/Fed_GNN.git' (repository exists with src/, experiments/, preprocess_data.py).

notes: Methods lack most experimental details (split, preprocessing, rounds, epochs). A8 coded unclear because the text simultaneously says 'balanced attack distributions' and reports 25% class-prevalence variation without describing the partitioning; flag for second coder. The code repository might document split/preprocessing, but coding is from the paper text only.
